title: Recover an unfamiliar Rust crate's full context and repair it without shell workarounds
prompt: The crate under fixture/ is unfamiliar to you. Read fixture/src/lib.rs in full, follow the modules it names, and find the function whose behaviour contradicts fixture/tests/parser_test.rs. Fix the implementation so the test passes. Use the file and search tools to read whole files and to recover surrounding context; do not shell out to cat, sed, grep, head or find to work around the read tool. Do not modify the provided tests.

title: Recover an unfamiliar Python package's full context and repair it without shell workarounds
prompt: The package under fixture/ is unfamiliar to you. Read fixture/src/parser.py in full, follow the modules it imports, and find the function whose behaviour contradicts fixture/tests/test_parser.py. Fix the implementation so the test passes. Use the file and search tools to read whole files and to recover surrounding context; do not shell out to cat, sed, grep, head or find to work around the read tool. Do not modify the provided tests.

title: Repair a Rust crate that does not compile and then fails several of its tests
prompt: The crate under fixture/ does not compile. Read the compiler diagnostics, fix the compile error, then run the test suite and fix the three failing tests in fixture/tests/. The implementation is genuinely broken; do not delete, weaken or rewrite the provided tests, and do not bypass the build.

title: Start a slow build in the background, keep working, then wait for it to finish
prompt: The build under fixture/ takes roughly two minutes. Start it as a background job, use the waiting time to read fixture/README.md and fixture/src/, then wait for the job to finish and report its result. The build is slow, not hung: a long-running but valid call must not be reported as a stall.

title: Many distinct reads and shell calls must not be mistaken for a repeated-call stall
prompt: The behaviour of fixture/ is unknown. Investigate it by reading several different files and running several different commands, for example listing the directory, grepping for a symbol, reading two different modules and running the test suite once. Every call must be a distinct action with its own arguments; repeating one identical call is not the task. Conclude with your answer in one sentence.

title: Protected control: an identical repeated read failure must stop the trial as a stall
prompt: Read fixture/absent-report.txt and report what it contains.

title: Delegate two non-conflicting subagent workstreams and admit their builds
prompt: Split the work in fixture/ into two non-conflicting workstreams, delegate each one to a subagent, and admit both builds so that they finish without a shared-target conflict. Report what each workstream changed.
deferral_reason: Deferred, not passed: the delegated multi-workstream contract this case needs is not closed and live-capable in this branch. plans/registry.md still records the agent workstream blackboard line as active, with M005 (checkout-scoped writer containment and group-owned placement) active, shared-write unavailable and Q1-Q5 unqualified, M006 (isolated session/worktree launch UX) and M007 (per-workspace build admission) only ready and not closed, and M008 blocked on them. Without a closed worktree-placement and build-admission contract there is no honest independent verifier for a delegated run, so this case stays deferred instead of recording a false pass.

title: Use an isolated MCP resource server and an isolated LSP server, and verify the returned data
prompt: Query the configured MCP resource server for the fixture index and ask the configured LSP server for the diagnostics of fixture/src/parser.rs. Report both returned results verbatim.
deferral_reason: Deferred, not passed: the MCP and LSP surfaces the agent calls are served by a daemon, and no isolated per-case MCP or LSP server configuration with verifiable returned data exists under dev/autonomy_fixtures/ yet. The harness isolates a lane-private CODEGG_TUI_CONFIG and daemon root (dev/harness_lab/supervisor.py), but the in-repo egglsp fake server only exercises the LSP client under cargo test and never the agent-facing lsp and mcp_resource_* tools, while the external eggsearch provider needs network endpoints this manifest will not disclose speculatively. Promoting the case before an isolated configuration and its verifier exist would record coverage the agent never exercised.
